name: Accenture
key_signal: ACN has cratered nearly 50% over the past six months (now $143.57 vs a 52-week high of $291) on fears over AI disruption and federal contract cuts, yet still trades at just 11.5x trailing / 9.8x forward earnings with a 24% ROE.
thesis: The valuation reset is severe enough to price in a lot of bad news: trailing P/E of 11.5x and forward P/E under 10x are unusually cheap for a company generating 17% operating margins, 24% ROE, and $12B in free cash flow on $73B revenue, while still growing revenue (+5.6%) and earnings (+9%) and now yielding 4.5%. MACD histogram has turned positive and RSI sits at a neutral 50, suggesting the freefall (mom_63d -25%, mom_126d -49%) may be stabilizing, and low leverage (debt/equity 25) gives balance-sheet flexibility to keep buying back stock and paying the dividend through the downturn. Consensus sell-side rating remains 'buy' across 25 analysts, indicating the Street hasn't capitulated on the long-term consulting franchise despite the price collapse.
bear_case: The technical picture is unambiguously broken — price is below both the 50-day ($156.55) and 200-day ($211.88) moving averages with no golden cross, and a 49% six-month drawdown of this magnitude in a large-cap IT services name reflects a genuine re-rating of the business model, not just sentiment: GenAI is increasingly seen as a substitute for the staff-augmentation and systems-integration work that has been Accenture's bread and butter, and federal government spending cuts (DOGE-driven) directly hit its large public-sector practice, which could structurally impair the revenue growth and margin assumptions embedded in that 'cheap' forward P/E — cheapness that can persist or deepen if bookings and guidance keep deteriorating, making this a classic value trap rather than a bottom.
